around.headline: Youth Congress leader manhandles DCP, actor Prakash Raj detained as SIR protests hit Bengaluru
around.summary: A Youth Congress functionary was seen manhandling a DCP during a Bengaluru protest, and actor-activist Prakash Raj was among those detained at an 'Election Commission Chalo' march against the ongoing electoral-roll revision, per NDTV and The Times of India. Expect heavier police presence and possible route diversions near protest sites in the city centre this week.

around.headline: Bikers push back against September 4 flyover ban; police defend the move
around.summary: Riders' groups are contesting the upcoming ban on two-wheelers and autos across five city flyovers, while traffic police are defending it on safety and accident-reduction grounds, per The Times of India. The restriction still takes effect in three days regardless, so plan an alternate route if your commute uses one of the listed corridors.

around.headline: BDA opens applications for Karanth Layout sites at roughly ₹72 lakh, first allotment in 18 years
around.summary: The Bengaluru Development Authority has begun accepting applications for sites in Dr. K. Shivaram Karanth Layout, priced at about ₹6,000/sq ft (roughly ₹72 lakh for a 30x40 site) — the first allotment for original land losers after an 18-year wait, per Deccan Herald and The Hindu. Worth checking if you've been waiting on a BDA site or are house-hunting in the northern suburbs.

around.headline: Karnataka recovers only 36% of ₹117 crore wrongly paid to dead Gruha Lakshmi beneficiaries
around.summary: The state has clawed back just over a third of the ₹117 crore mistakenly disbursed under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme to beneficiaries who had already died, per The Times of India. If a family member enrolled in a welfare scheme passes away, reporting it promptly to the local office can save the household a recovery notice later.

around.headline: MLA alleges payment-quota, bribery system entrenched in Karnataka administration
around.summary: A sitting MLA has publicly alleged that a payment-quota and bribery system runs through routine government processes in Karnataka, per The Times of India. No department specifics yet, but worth keeping receipts and escalating in writing if any state office asks for unofficial payments.

around.headline: Nepal-China floods kill over 1,000; 13 people from Karnataka still untraced
around.summary: Floods triggered by heavy rain across Nepal and China have killed more than 1,000 people, and 13 people from Karnataka remain untraced among those affected, per AP News and The Times of India. If you have family or friends travelling in Nepal, it's worth checking in on them directly rather than waiting for official word.
around.source: AP News, The Times of India

street_smart.title: A friend forwards you a 'guaranteed instant loan, no paperwork, cash in 10 minutes' app ahead of payday, saying they used it themselves last month with zero issues. You're about to install it, and it's asking for your contacts, gallery and SMS permissions before it will let you apply. What do you check first?
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds fit the choice-based trap format cleanly (today's real Bengaluru/India stories — SIR-protest scuffles, a flyover-ban pushback, a BDA land allotment, Gruha Lakshmi recovery, an MLA's bribery allegation, and the Nepal-China floods — are civic, administrative, or tragedy-driven rather than personal decision points). Rotating in from the evergreen list: loan-app harassment, the least recently used evergreen topic (last appeared 2026-08-15, 17 days ago) — but with a different mechanism this time: vetting an app *before* installing it, not responding to blackmail *after* falling for one, which was the 08-15 angle. Every other evergreen topic has run more recently: digital-arrest (08-28), UPI fraud (08-26), auto/cab overcharging (08-26), rental traps and tenant rights (09-01, this morning), fake job offers (08-31), OTP/social engineering (08-29), two-wheeler theft (08-27), medical emergencies (08-31), consumer court (08-18), phone snatching (08-28), and credit-card skimming (08-16).
street_smart.situation: Payday is still four days out, you have a genuine short-term cash crunch, and the app promises approval in minutes with 'no paperwork' — but it wants permissions no bank loan form ever asks for.

choices.text: Install it right away since your friend vouches for it, and grant the contacts, gallery and SMS permissions it asks for so the approval goes through faster.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Many predatory instant-loan apps run smoothly for early borrowers — that's how they build trust and referrals — and only turn abusive once a payment is late. Your friend's good experience isn't proof the app is a licensed lender, and the contacts/gallery access you just granted is exactly what lets these apps threaten your entire phonebook later.

choices.text: Cross-check the lender's name on the RBI's Sachet portal (sachet.rbi.org.in) or the RBI's list of registered NBFCs, install only the verified official listing, and refuse the contacts, gallery and SMS permissions during setup.
choices.feedback: Correct. Every legitimate digital lender in India is either a bank/NBFC or explicitly partnered with one, and RBI's Sachet portal tracks and flags unregistered lending apps. No legitimate lender needs your contact list or photos to disburse or recover a loan — refusing those permissions blocks the exact mechanism predatory apps use to harass you if you're ever late.

choices.text: Judge it by its Play Store star rating and download count before installing.
choices.feedback: Risky. Ratings and install counts are easy to inflate, and several apps later flagged by RBI or police for harassment still had thousands of downloads and decent ratings before the complaints piled up. A Play Store listing is not proof of RBI registration.

choices.text: Grant the permissions to get approved, then revoke them or uninstall the app right after, assuming that removes its access to your data.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Once an app has synced your contacts, gallery or messages to its servers, uninstalling it or revoking the permission afterward doesn't delete what it already copied — the data harvest happens the moment you grant access, not continuously while the app stays installed.

takeaways: Before installing any instant-loan app, verify the lender against RBI's Sachet portal (sachet.rbi.org.in) or the RBI's list of registered NBFCs — a Play Store listing alone is not proof of legitimacy.
Never grant a loan app access to your contacts, gallery or SMS — legitimate lenders don't need them to disburse or recover a loan, and the data can be used against you even after you uninstall.
If you're already facing harassment from an app you installed, report it immediately to the National Cyber Crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in — documented screenshots make a takedown faster.

quiz.question: Per today's news, roughly how much would a resident pay for a 30x40 site in BDA's newly opened Dr. K. Shivaram Karanth Layout allotment?
quiz.why: The sites are priced at around ₹6,000/sq ft, and this is the first allotment for original land losers after an 18-year wait.

quiz.question: According to today's report, what share of the ₹117 crore wrongly paid to dead beneficiaries under Karnataka's Gruha Lakshmi scheme has been recovered so far?
quiz.why: Gruha Lakshmi pays ₹2,000 a month to women heads of eligible households; overpayments to deceased beneficiaries have proven hard to claw back statewide.

quiz.question: Floods have killed over 1,000 people across Nepal and China. Per today's report, how many people from Karnataka are still untraced?
quiz.why: Many of those affected were travellers and trekkers, which is why states like Karnataka are tracking their own residents separately from the national toll.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's municipal water supply is primarily piped in from which river, over 100 km away?
quiz.why: The Cauvery Water Supply Scheme pumps water uphill from the river to the city, making it one of India's most energy-intensive urban water systems.

quiz.question: In lending, what does the 'NBFC' in 'RBI-registered NBFC' stand for?
quiz.why: NBFCs can lend money like banks but can't accept demand deposits — checking a lender's NBFC registration on RBI's Sachet portal is a quick way to spot an unlicensed loan app.
